title: Write-once custody bundler for admin audit logs with per-region residency and integrity proofs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: produce tamper-evident, write-once custody bundles for admin audit logs (admin actions, privileged access, configuration changes) that enforce regional data residency and retention policies, provide cryptographic integrity proofs, and automate evidence/reporting for compliance teams. Scope: exporter service that creates daily/rolling custody bundles per-account-per-region, fingerprints entries into a Merkle tree, stamps bundle manifests via customer KMS/HSM or Redwood signing key, writes bundles to immutable WORM-capable object stores (S3 Object Lock or on-prem WORM appliance), and emits a metadata index for query and legal-hold exports. Non-goals: replacing live audit stream or changing ingest pipeline; we will consume existing audit event streams (Kafka/stream).
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a given account and region, the bundler produces a compressed archive (tar.gz) containing all admin audit events for the bucketed period with an accompanying manifest.json that lists per-entry SHA256 hashes and a Merkle root. 2) Manifest is signed with either customer KMS key (when provided) or Redwood signing key; signature verified by verifier utility. 3) Bundle stored into object store with Object Lock/Governance or WORM mode enabled; retention metadata applied per customer residency policy. 4) Index record emitted to Audit Evidence Index service with hashed pointers (no plaintext duplication) and queryable by compliance console. 5) API to request legal-hold export that returns notarized bundle and verification chain. 6) End-to-end tests demonstrate detection of tampering (manifest mismatch) and automatic re-ingest/fallback alerts.
implementation_notes: - Input: subscribe to admin-audit Kafka topic; support backfill from parquet snapshot for initial seeding. - Partitioning: per-tenant, per-region, daily windows with configurable rollup (hourly for high-volume tenants). - Merkle tree built with canonicalized JSON entries (stable field ordering) to avoid signature churn. - Signing: integrate with KMS Sign API and HSM for on-prem; fallback to Redwood key stored in HSM when customer key absent. - Storage: S3 Object Lock (compliance mode) for hosted; for Private deployment, integrate with NFS WORM appliance or immutability driver. - Metadata: store minimal index rows (tenant_id, region, window_start, window_end, merkle_root, object_uri, signature, retention_until) and expose via Console. - Security: ensure no plaintext audit duplication outside the bundle; use envelope encryption with per-tenant data keys. - Quotas & rate limits: throttle bundling jobs for very high-volume tenants; rotate to hourly windows on demand.
rollout_plan: 1) Prototype: local bundler tool + unit tests (2 weeks). 2) Integration: connect to staging Kafka, sign with staging KMS, push to staging S3 Object Lock (2 weeks). 3) Canary: enable for 5 low-volume tenants in hosted region-us-west-2, monitor bundle consistency and storage costs (2 weeks). 4) Gradual ramp: increase tenant coverage, enable per-tenant KMS when requested; add legal-hold exports and UI. 5) Private: ship agent version for VPC/on-prem with HSM signing support. Monitor: error rate, manifest verification failures, storage retention drift, compliance report generation latency.
qa_and_test_plan: - Unit: hashing, canonicalization, merkle construction, manifest signing/verification. - Integration: end-to-end test in staging linking Kafka -> bundler -> signed bundle -> storage -> index -> verifier. - Attack sims: modify stored bundle to ensure verifier catches tamper and incident is created. - Scale test: run synthetic high-volume tenant to validate hourly rollups and queueing. - Compliance sign-off: legal/compliance to validate manifest fields and export process. - Performance: ensure bundling job finishes within SLA for daily window (configurable), and partial bundle streaming for very large windows.
